docs.title: Public Market POS — Technical Docs
docs.text:
Public Market POS ("SnapStock") is a mobile-first point-of-sale and inventory app for sellers in public markets and small retail (sari-sari stores, market stalls), with a companion buyer experience for digital orders, receipts, and messaging.

This site documents the system for developers working on the codebase. For the full product spec and the reasoning behind schema decisions, see pos-system-build-plan.md in the repo root. For end-user instructions, see the standalone user manuals in /docs-manuals (not part of this site — see Deferred Features and the repo README for details on why those are kept separate).

docs.title: Tech stack
docs.text: Layer Technology Backend framework FastAPI ORM / migrations SQLAlchemy · Alembic Database PostgreSQL Auth JWT (python-jose), passlib/bcrypt password hashing Rate limiting slowapi Frontend framework React 19 (Vite) Routing React Router Server state TanStack Query HTTP client Axios Charts Recharts QR codes qrcode.react

docs.title: Repo structure
docs.text:
backend/
├── app/
│   ├── core/         # auth deps (get_current_user, require_seller, require_buyer), security, rate limiting, business_time
│   ├── models/        # SQLAlchemy models — one file per domain
│   ├── routers/       # FastAPI routers — auth, request/response wiring only
│   ├── schemas/        # Pydantic request/response models (CamelModel base)
│   ├── services/       # business logic — inventory, sales, catalog, messages, payouts, uploads, analytics/ (package)
│   ├── config.py       # Settings (env-driven)
│   ├── database.py     # SQLAlchemy engine/session
│   └── main.py         # FastAPI app, router mounting, CORS, rate limit handler
├── alembic/            # migrations
├── scripts/seed.py      # demo data seeding
└── tests/               # pytest suite (requires local Postgres)

frontend/
├── src/
│   ├── api/            # axios wrappers, one file per backend resource
│   ├── features/       # auth, inventory, sales, analytics, dashboard, messages, payouts, buyer
│   ├── components/     # shared UI primitives (Badge, StatTile, QuantityStepper, ...)
│   ├── hooks/
│   └── lib/            # apiClient, i18n, nav, dates, offlineQueue, format helpers
├── index.html
└── vite.config.js      # dev server proxy: /api and /uploads → backend on 6767

docs-technical/   # this site
docs-manuals/     # standalone Word-conversion-ready user manuals (sellers, buyers)
docker-compose.yml # local Postgres 16 for development

docs.title: Three app surfaces, one backend
docs.text:
• Seller app — inventory (categories, costs, bulk restock), walk-in checkout, approving buyers' online orders, transactions, the analytics hub, payout accounts, messaging. Routes gated by ProtectedRoute role="seller".
  • Buyer app — catalog browsing, placing orders and uploading payment screenshots, digital receipts, messaging sellers. Routes gated by ProtectedRoute role="buyer".
  • Backend API — a single FastAPI app (app/main.py) exposing all routers under /api/v1, backed by one shared PostgreSQL database. See Architecture Overview.

Continue to Getting Started to run the stack locally, or Architecture Overview for how the pieces fit together.

docs.title: Database Schema
docs.text:
PostgreSQL, accessed through SQLAlchemy models in backend/app/models/. Every table uses a UUID primary key and UTC-aware timestamps via the shared mixins in models/mixins.py (UUIDPkMixin, CreatedAtMixin, UpdatedAtMixin).

erDiagram
    USERS ||--o| SELLER_PROFILES : "has (if role=seller)"
    SELLER_PROFILES ||--o{ SELLER_PAYOUT_ACCOUNTS : "receives payments via"
    USERS ||--o{ PRODUCTS : "sells (seller_id)"
    USERS ||--o{ SALES : "sells as (seller_id)"
    USERS |o--o{ SALES : "buys as (buyer_id, nullable)"
    USERS ||--o{ CONVERSATIONS : "participates as seller"
    USERS ||--o{ CONVERSATIONS : "participates as buyer"
    USERS ||--o{ MESSAGES : "sends (sender_id)"

    PRODUCTS ||--o{ SALE_ITEMS : "sold as (product_id, nullable)"
    PRODUCTS ||--o{ STOCK_MOVEMENTS : "tracked by"
    PRODUCTS ||--o{ PRODUCT_COST_HISTORY : "cost logged in"
    PRODUCTS |o--o{ CONVERSATIONS : "discussed in (product_id, nullable)"

    SALES ||--o{ SALE_ITEMS : "contains"
    SALES |o--o{ STOCK_MOVEMENTS : "caused (sale_id, nullable)"

    SALES |o--o{ MESSAGES : "order card (sale_id, nullable)"

    CONVERSATIONS ||--o{ MESSAGES : "contains"

    USERS {
        uuid id PK
        string email UK
        string hashed_password
        string full_name
        enum role "seller | buyer"
        string phone
        string preferred_language
        bool is_active
        string qr_login_key_hash UK "sha256 of the login QR key"
        timestamptz qr_login_created_at
    }
    SELLER_PROFILES {
        uuid id PK
        uuid user_id FK "unique -> users.id"
        string business_name
        enum business_type "wholesale | retail | both"
        text address
        text description
    }
    SELLER_PAYOUT_ACCOUNTS {
        uuid id PK
        uuid seller_profile_id FK "-> seller_profiles.id, cascade delete"
        enum method "gcash | maya | bank_transfer | other (never cash)"
        string account_name
        string account_number
        string bank_name "NULLABLE: bank, or provider for other"
        string qr_url "NULLABLE"
        bool is_default
    }
    PRODUCTS {
        uuid id PK
        uuid seller_id FK "-> users.id"
        string name
        int price_cents
        int cost_cents "NULLABLE: unit cost, same unit as price"
        enum unit_type "piece | bundle | measure"
        string unit_label "measure only: kg, yd, m, ..."
        int pieces_per_unit
        int stock_pieces "pieces; thousandths of unit for measure"
        int low_stock_threshold
        string category
        bool is_active "soft delete"
    }
    SALES {
        uuid id PK
        uuid seller_id FK "-> users.id"
        uuid buyer_id FK "-> users.id, NULLABLE"
        enum sale_type "itemized | walk_in"
        int subtotal_cents "sum of line totals at charged prices"
        int discount_cents "sale-level, default 0"
        int total_cents "subtotal - discount"
        enum status "completed | voided | refunded | pending_payment | cancelled"
        timestamptz status_changed_at "NULLABLE"
        text status_reason "NULLABLE, seller-only"
        enum payment_method
        string receipt_code UK
        text note
        string payment_proof_url "NULLABLE: buyer's screenshot, never public"
        timestamptz proof_submitted_at "NULLABLE"
    }
    SALE_ITEMS {
        uuid id PK
        uuid sale_id FK "-> sales.id, cascade delete"
        uuid product_id FK "-> products.id, NULLABLE"
        string product_name_snapshot
        int list_price_cents_snapshot "product price at sale time"
        int unit_price_cents_snapshot "price actually charged"
        int unit_cost_cents_snapshot "NULLABLE: cost at sale time"
        int cost_total_cents "NULLABLE: line COGS"
        int quantity
        enum unit_type_snapshot
        string unit_label_snapshot
        int pieces_deducted
        int line_total_cents
    }
    STOCK_MOVEMENTS {
        uuid id PK
        uuid product_id FK "-> products.id"
        int change_pieces "signed: + restock, - sale"
        enum reason "sale | quick_sell | restock | correction | initial | void | refund | cancel"
        uuid sale_id FK "-> sales.id, NULLABLE"
        text note
    }
    PRODUCT_COST_HISTORY {
        uuid id PK
        uuid product_id FK "-> products.id"
        int cost_cents
        enum source "manual | restock"
    }
    CONVERSATIONS {
        uuid id PK
        uuid seller_id FK "-> users.id"
        uuid buyer_id FK "-> users.id"
        uuid product_id FK "-> products.id, NULLABLE"
        timestamptz last_message_at
    }
    MESSAGES {
        uuid id PK
        uuid conversation_id FK "-> conversations.id"
        uuid sender_id FK "-> users.id"
        text body
        uuid sale_id FK "-> sales.id, NULLABLE: order card"
        timestamptz read_at "NULL until read"
    }

docs.title: Why buyer_id is nullable
docs.text: sales.buyer_id is nullable because sale_type = walk_in (an anonymous cash sale rung up at the stall, with no buyer account involved) and sale_type = itemized (a buyer-linked digital order) share one table. A walk-in sale simply never sets buyer_id; SaleCreate.check_consistency enforces the pairing at the API boundary (itemized requires a buyer_id, walk_in forbids one). Both sale types deduct stock and count toward analytics identically — no code branches on sale_type for that shared behavior, only for what's required on the way in and what's shown on receipts (buyer name vs. "Walk-in").

docs.title: Other notable design choices
docs.text:
• sale_items.product_id is nullable and the row snapshots product_name_snapshot, unit_price_cents_snapshot, unit_type_snapshot, unit_label_snapshot at write time. Products are soft-deleted (is_active = false) only — never hard-deleted, because sale_items (and therefore every past receipt) references them by ID. The snapshot columns mean a receipt's wording and price never change even if the product is later renamed or re-priced.
  • stock_movements is append-only and is the audit trail for every change to products.stock_pieces. services.inventory.apply_stock_change is the only code path allowed to write stock_pieces, and it always writes a matching stock_movements row (with sale_id set when the change came from a sale, null for a manual restock).
  • conversations has a uniqueness constraint on (seller_id, buyer_id, product_id) so re-opening a chat about the same product with the same counterpart reuses the existing thread.
  • sales.status covers buyer orders too. A buyer's online order is a normal itemized sale created as pending_payment (stock already reserved), which becomes completed when the seller confirms payment or cancelled (stock returned with a cancel movement) when either side backs out. Analytics count only completed (plus refunded for gross sales and refunds).
  • messages.sale_id marks an order card, the message posted from the buyer when their order is ready for review. The API attaches the order's live status to it.
  • seller_payout_accounts.method reuses the payment_method enum, so a buyer's chosen method maps straight to the seller's matching accounts. The schema layer keeps cash out.
  • All money is integer cents (price_cents, total_cents, etc.) — there are no floating-point currency columns anywhere in the schema.

docs.title: Deferred Features
docs.text: Things that are stubbed, out-of-scope, or intentionally simplified in the current implementation — called out here so they aren't mistaken for bugs.

docs.title: Payment gateway integration
docs.text: payment_method (cash | gcash | maya | bank_transfer | other) is recorded on every sale, but there is no integration with GCash, Maya, or any bank/card processor. Sellers list where they get paid as payout accounts (account details plus a QR image), and buyers pay outside the app. For a digital online order, the buyer uploads a screenshot of the payment and the seller checks it by eye before tapping Confirm payment. Nothing in the backend captures, verifies or reconciles the money itself.

docs.title: Real-time messaging
docs.text: app/routers/messages.py is a plain REST API — there is no WebSocket, SSE, or push channel. The frontend polls: ConversationListPage and ChatPage refetch every 6–8 seconds via TanStack Query's refetchInterval. This is adequate for a low-frequency market-stall chat but is not real-time delivery.

docs.title: Vision-based image search
docs.text:
POST /catalog/search-by-image (app/routers/catalog.py) and its seller-side twin POST /products/search-by-image (app/routers/inventory.py) accept and validate an uploaded photo (JPEG/PNG/WebP) but do not analyze it. The code comment in the router spells out the intent:

Stage 1: the photo is accepted but not analyzed — it's a shortcut into a pre-filled text search the buyer confirms. Stage 2 swaps this matching step for real vision search without changing the request/response shape.

Today both run a keyword search on the query form field and return those results with confidence: null on every item — the photo itself has no effect on the results.

docs.title: Multi-staff accounts
docs.text: Each User row with role = seller has exactly one SellerProfile (a single stall/business identity). There is no concept of multiple staff logins under one stall, staff permission tiers, or an owner/employee distinction — whoever holds the seller account's credentials has full access to that stall's inventory, sales, and messages.

docs.title: Full offline-first sync
docs.text:
frontend/src/lib/offlineQueue.js provides partial resilience, not full offline-first support: it queues quick-sell requests in localStorage when a request fails with a network error (no response reaching the server — not a rejection like insufficient stock), and replays them on reconnect, stopping at the first entry that still fails on the network but dropping entries the server actively rejects. Browsing, checkout, approving orders, messaging, and every other action still require a live connection — there is no general offline cache or conflict-resolution layer.

The queue currently gets no new entries: the quick-sell screen (QuickSellSheet.jsx) isn't mounted anywhere and nothing calls enqueueQuickSell. InventoryPage still replays any queued entries when it loads and when the browser comes back online. Walk-in sales made through the New Sale cart are not queued at all.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This runs the backend, database migrations, and frontend locally. Backend serves on port 6767, frontend dev server on 5173, in separate terminals.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.11+ and PostgreSQL on localhost:5432 (user/pass postgres/postgres). The repo's docker-compose.yml provides one: docker compose up -d db from the repo root starts Postgres 16 with data in the snapstock-pgdata volume (development only).
  • Node.js for the frontend

docs.title: Backend
docs.text:
cd backend
python -m venv .venv
.venv/Scripts/activate        # Windows
# source .venv/bin/activate   # macOS/Linux
pip install -r requirements.txt

Create backend/.env (defaults work for local Postgres):

DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg2://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/pos_system
SECRET_KEY=dev-secret-key-change-in-production
ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES=1440
CORS_ORIGINS=["http://localhost:5173"]
UPLOAD_DIR=uploads
BUSINESS_TIMEZONE=Asia/Manila

BUSINESS_TIMEZONE (IANA name, default Asia/Manila) defines the sellers' business day for "today", date ranges and daily/weekday/hourly analytics buckets. tzdata is in requirements.txt so this works on Windows too. AUTH_REGISTER_RATE_LIMIT (default 5/minute) and AUTH_LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT (default 10/minute) are also configurable.

Apply migrations, then run the server:

alembic upgrade head
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 6767
  • Health check: GET http://localhost:6767/api/v1/health → {"status": "ok"}
  • Interactive API docs (Swagger UI): http://localhost:6767/docs

docs.title: Seed demo data
docs.text: python scripts/seed.py

docs.title: Run tests
docs.text:
pytest

Tests require a live Postgres on localhost:5432. tests/conftest.py auto-creates a separate pos_system_test database, applies Base.metadata.create_all for the session, and truncates all tables between tests.

docs.title: New migrations
docs.text:
alembic revision --autogenerate -m "message"
alembic upgrade head
alembic downgrade base   # reverse all, if needed

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text:
cd frontend
npm install

frontend/.env:

VITE_API_URL=/api/v1

The URL is relative on purpose. The Vite dev server (vite.config.js) proxies /api and /uploads to the backend at http://127.0.0.1:6767 and listens on all interfaces (server.host: true). A phone on the same Wi-Fi can open http://<your-PC-IP>:5173 and only needs to reach that one port. Because requests are same-origin through the proxy, CORS doesn't come into play in development. If you point VITE_API_URL at an absolute URL instead, add the frontend's origin to the backend's CORS_ORIGINS.

Run the dev server:

npm run dev

Loads at http://localhost:5173.

npm run lint   # oxlint, not eslint
npm run build

docs.title: Running both
docs.text: Start the backend (uvicorn, port 6767) and the frontend (npm run dev, port 5173) in separate terminals, then open http://localhost:5173 (or http://<your-PC-IP>:5173 on a phone). The frontend's apiClient sends requests to VITE_API_URL (/api/v1), and the Vite proxy forwards them to the backend.

docs.title: Inventory Service
docs.text:
Owns Product data and all stock changes. Router: app/routers/inventory.py (prefix /products), business logic in app/services/inventory.py. All endpoints below require Authorization: Bearer <token> and require_seller (the caller must own the product — enforced by filtering on seller.id, not a separate permission check).

Money fields are integer cents (priceCents). All request/response bodies are camelCase on the wire (Pydantic CamelModel auto-converts to/from the backend's snake_case).

docs.title: GET /products/low-stock
docs.text: Returns products where stock_pieces <= low_stock_threshold, ordered by stock_pieces ascending. Response: list[ProductRead].

docs.title: GET /products/categories and DELETE /products/categories
docs.text:
GET returns the distinct, non-empty category values across the caller's active products, sorted case-insensitively (list[str]). There is no categories table: a category exists while at least one product uses it. The frontend's CategorySelect lets sellers pick one, type a new one, or delete one.

DELETE /products/categories?name=<category> clears that category from every active product of the caller (sets it to null). Returns 204.

docs.title: GET /products
docs.text:
List/search the caller's products.

Query params: search (name substring), category, stock_status (in_stock | low | out), page (default 1), pageSize (default 20, max 100).

Response: ProductListResponse — { items: ProductRead[], total, page, pageSize }.

ProductRead includes costCents (seller-only, null if unknown) and a computed stockStatus (in_stock | low | out).

docs.title: POST /products
docs.text:
Create a product. stock_pieces = 0 initially; if stockPieces > 0 is supplied, it's applied via apply_stock_change with reason initial (so it still generates an audit row).

Request (ProductCreate):

Field Type Notes name string required description string | null priceCents int required, > 0 costCents int | null ≥ 0. What one selling unit costs the seller. Used for profit; recorded in product_cost_history unitType piece | bundle | measure required unitLabel string | null ≤ 16 chars. Required for measure (422 otherwise), e.g. kg, yd; ignored/cleared for other types piecesPerUnit int default 1, ≥ 1. Must be 1 unless unitType = bundle (400 otherwise) stockPieces int default 0, ≥ 0. Thousandths of the unit for measure lowStockThreshold int default 10, ≥ 0. Thousandths of the unit for measure category string | null

Response: ProductRead (201).

docs.title: GET /products/{productId}
docs.text: Fetch one owned product. 404 if not found, not owned, or soft-deleted (is_active = false).

docs.title: PATCH /products/{productId}
docs.text: Partial update (ProductUpdate — same fields as create, all optional, exclude_unset applied). Does not accept stockPieces — stock is only ever changed via quick-sell, sale, or restock. A changed costCents goes through set_product_cost (source manual), which appends a product_cost_history row. Past profit is unaffected, because sales keep their own cost snapshot.

docs.title: DELETE /products/{productId}
docs.text: Soft-delete only: sets is_active = false. Returns 204. Products are never hard-deleted because sale_items.product_id references them and past receipts must keep resolving.

docs.title: POST /products/{productId}/quick-sell
docs.text:
The single-tap walk-in sale path (see Data Flow). Creates a walk_in sale with buyer_id = null and deducts stock in one transaction.

Request (QuickSellRequest): { quantity: int (>0), paymentMethod: cash|gcash|maya|bank_transfer|other, unitPriceCents?: int }

Response (QuickSellResult): { product: ProductRead, saleId, receiptCode, totalCents }

Errors: 400 if stock_pieces − quantity × piecesPerUnit < 0 (InsufficientStockError).

Note

The current frontend has no quick-sell screen: QuickSellSheet.jsx and api/products.quickSellProduct exist but nothing mounts or calls them. Walk-in sales go through the New Sale cart (POST /sales). The endpoint and its tests are still in place.

docs.title: POST /products/{productId}/restock
docs.text:
Increases stock. Writes a stock_movements row with reason restock.

Request (RestockRequest): { quantity: int (>0), note?: string, unitCostCents?: int }. unitCostCents is the cost per selling unit for this delivery. If given, it becomes the product's cost (product_cost_history source restock). If omitted, the cost stays the same.

Response: ProductRead.

docs.title: POST /products/restock
docs.text:
Restock several products in one go (the Restock Items screen, RestockPicker.jsx).

Request (BulkRestockRequest): { items: { productId, quantity (>0), unitCostCents? }[] (min 1), note?: string }

Duplicate productIds are summed. Every product is resolved before any stock changes, so one unknown or foreign ID fails the whole batch with 404. Each product gets its own restock movement, plus a cost update when unitCostCents is given. Response: list[ProductRead].

docs.title: POST /products/search-by-image
docs.text:
Seller-side mirror of the catalog photo search, scoped to the caller's own products. Multipart file (JPEG/PNG/WebP) plus a query form field (min length 1). Stage 1: the photo is validated but not analyzed, and results are a keyword search on query (first 20 matches).

Response (ProductImageSearchResponse): { query, results: { product: ProductRead, confidence: null }[] }. Errors: 400 (not an image).

docs.title: POST /products/{productId}/photo
docs.text:
Multipart upload (file), JPEG/PNG/WebP only. Saves to UPLOAD_DIR under {productId}_{random8hex}{ext} and sets photoUrl to /uploads/{filename} (served statically — see app.mount("/uploads", ...) in app/main.py). Validation and saving live in app/services/uploads.py (validate_image, save_image), which payout QR codes and payment screenshots use as well.

Response: ProductRead.

docs.title: Buyer-facing catalog reads (app/routers/catalog.py)
docs.text:
Read-only browsing of the same Product data, no auth required. Prefix: none (mounted at /api/v1 root, tag catalog).

Method & path Description GET /catalog/products List active products across all sellers. Query: search, category, sellerId, page, pageSize. Returns CatalogProductListResponse (includes sellerName, stockStatus, but no seller/internal IDs beyond sellerId). GET /catalog/products/{productId} Single product, CatalogProductRead. 404 if missing. GET /catalog/sellers/{sellerId} Seller's public profile + active listings, CatalogSellerRead. POST /catalog/search-by-image Multipart file + query form field. Stage 1 stub: the photo is accepted (validated as JPEG/PNG/WebP) but not analyzed — it's a shortcut into a keyword search on query. See Deferred Features. Returns ImageSearchResponse with confidence: null on every result.

Ordering (POST /catalog/products/{productId}/order) and buyer receipts (GET /me/receipts) are documented in Sales Service, since they're powered by the sales service, not inventory.

docs.title: Messaging Service
docs.text:
One-to-one conversations between a seller and a buyer, optionally pinned to a product. Router: app/routers/messages.py (prefix /conversations), business logic in app/services/messages.py. All endpoints require Authorization: Bearer <token> (get_current_user — either role, not seller/buyer-restricted) and are scoped to conversations the caller participates in.

A (seller_id, buyer_id, product_id) triple is unique (uq_conversations_seller_buyer_product) — starting a new conversation with the same counterpart about the same product returns the existing one instead of creating a duplicate.

docs.title: GET /conversations
docs.text:
List the caller's conversations (as either the seller or buyer side), newest activity first (last_message_at descending).

Response (ConversationListResponse): items[], each with otherUser (id, fullName, role), product (pinned product summary, or null), lastMessageAt, lastMessagePreview, unreadCount, createdAt.

docs.title: POST /conversations
docs.text:
Start (or resume) a conversation with another user, optionally about a specific product.

Request (ConversationCreate): { otherUserId: UUID, productId?: UUID }

Server-side, the seller/buyer sides are inferred from the caller's own role and the other user's role (a seller can only start a conversation with a buyer, and vice versa — _resolve_participants). If productId is given, it must be an active product belonging to the seller side of the conversation.

Response: ConversationRead (201). Errors: 404 if the other user or product doesn't resolve to a valid counterpart.

docs.title: GET /conversations/{conversationId}/messages
docs.text:
Paginated message history, newest first (page, pageSize, default 30/page, max 100).

Response: MessageListResponse — { items: MessageRead[], total, page, pageSize }. Each MessageRead has id, conversationId, senderId, body, createdAt, readAt (null until read), saleId and order. Both are null on ordinary messages.

Errors: 404 if the conversation doesn't exist or the caller isn't a participant.

docs.title: POST /conversations/{conversationId}/messages
docs.text:
Send a message. Also bumps conversation.last_message_at to now.

Request (MessageCreate): { body: string (min length 1) } Response: MessageRead (201).

docs.title: POST /conversations/{conversationId}/read
docs.text: Marks every message in the conversation not sent by the caller as read (read_at = now()). Used to zero out the unread badge when a conversation is opened. Returns 204, no body.

docs.title: Order cards
docs.text:
When a buyer's online order becomes ready for the seller to review, the backend posts a message from the buyer into their conversation with the seller (services/messages.post_order_card):

  • a cash order, as soon as it is placed;
  • a digital order (GCash, Maya, bank, other), each time the buyer uploads a payment screenshot.

The message goes into the conversation for that seller, buyer and the order's first product, and is created if it doesn't exist yet. Its body is plain text (e.g. "Ana bought Pork belly (₱350.00) and will pay in cash. Approve or not?"), so it reads correctly as a list preview. Its messages.sale_id points at the order.

GET .../messages attaches the order's live state as order (MessageOrder: id, buyerName, itemsSummary, totalCents, paymentMethod, status, paymentProofUrl). The card always shows the current status, even after the order was approved or cancelled. features/messages/OrderCardBubble.jsx renders it. While the order is pending, the seller gets Review & approve, which opens /sales?path=account&order=<id> (see Sales Service). Otherwise the button is View order, which takes the buyer to /buyer/orders/<id>.

Delivery is poll-based on the frontend (ConversationListPage/ChatPage refetch every 6–8s via TanStack Query's refetchInterval) — there is no WebSocket/push channel. See Deferred Features.

docs.title: Payout Accounts
docs.text:
Where a seller receives non-cash payments: their GCash, Maya, bank or other e-wallet accounts, each optionally with a QR code. Buyers see these accounts on the order page, and the seller can show the matching QR to a walk-in customer. Router: app/routers/payouts.py (prefix /seller/payout-accounts), business logic in app/services/payouts.py, model SellerPayoutAccount (app/models/payout_account.py).

All endpoints require Authorization: Bearer <token> and require_seller. Accounts hang off the seller's seller_profiles row, and every query filters by that profile, so a seller can only see and change their own accounts.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• method reuses the sales payment_method enum minus cash: gcash, maya, bank_transfer or other. Cash is never a payout account because buyers just hand it over.
  • bankName is required for bank_transfer (the bank) and other (the provider, e.g. GoTyme, ShopeePay). The schema rejects a missing one with 422.
  • Exactly one account is the default. The first account a seller creates becomes the default automatically, and setting isDefault: true on another account clears it everywhere else.
  • Lists come back default first, then oldest first.

PayoutAccountRead: id, method, accountName, accountNumber, bankName, qrUrl, isDefault.

docs.title: GET /seller/payout-accounts
docs.text: List the caller's accounts. Response: list[PayoutAccountRead].

docs.title: POST /seller/payout-accounts
docs.text:
Request (PayoutAccountCreate): { method, accountName, accountNumber, bankName?, isDefault? } (accountName and accountNumber are trimmed and must not be empty).

Response: PayoutAccountRead (201).

docs.title: PATCH /seller/payout-accounts/{accountId}
docs.text: Partial update (PayoutAccountUpdate, all fields optional). Errors: 404 if the account isn't the caller's; 422 if the change leaves a bank_transfer/other account without a bankName.

docs.title: DELETE /seller/payout-accounts/{accountId}
docs.text: Returns 204. Errors: 404.

docs.title: POST /seller/payout-accounts/{accountId}/qr
docs.text: Multipart file (JPEG/PNG/WebP), saved through services/uploads.save_image and stored as qrUrl (/uploads/...). Uploading again replaces the QR. Errors: 400 (not an image), 404.

docs.title: Where the accounts show up
docs.text:
• Buyer order page: GET /me/orders/{saleId} returns the seller's payoutAccounts, so the buyer can scan a QR or copy an account number before uploading their payment screenshot (see Sales Service).
  • Payment-method pickers: features/payouts/PaymentMethodPicker.jsx always offers Cash and greys out every other method the seller has no account for. It is used in the buyer's BuySheet and in the seller's walk-in PaymentSheet, where it shows the matching QR for the customer to scan.
  • Onboarding: after a seller registers, RegisterPage offers to add a first account (it can be skipped). Until the seller has one, the dashboard shows PayoutSetupBanner. Sellers manage accounts later under Profile → Payout accounts (PayoutAccountsSection).

docs.title: Sales Service
docs.text:
Owns Sale/SaleItem data and is the only writer of the sales table. Router: app/routers/sales.py (prefix /sales), business logic in app/services/sales.py. Stock deduction is delegated to the Inventory Service's apply_stock_change — see Architecture Overview.

All money fields are integer cents. All endpoints require Authorization: Bearer <token> and require_seller except GET /sales/receipt/{receiptCode}, which is the one public, unauthenticated endpoint in the whole API.

docs.title: GET /sales/buyers/search
docs.text:
Search registered buyers by name, email or phone. The current frontend doesn't call it, because the seller's New Sale → Buyer Account tab now only approves online orders (see below).

Query: q (min length 2). Response: list[BuyerSearchResult] (id, fullName, email, phone).

docs.title: POST /sales
docs.text:
Create a sale — either itemized (cart of products) or a walk-in lump sum with no line items.

Request (SaleCreate):

Field Type Notes saleType itemized | walk_in buyerId UUID | null required if itemized; must be null if walk_in paymentMethod cash|gcash|maya|bank_transfer|other items { productId, quantity, unitPriceCents?, byPiece? }[] required (non-empty) if itemized. unitPriceCents is the price agreed during the sale; omitted = the product's current price. It never changes the product. byPiece: true sells single pieces of a bundle product at bundle price ÷ pieces per bundle (400 for other unit types); see Unit Conversion. POST /catalog/products/{id}/order takes the same optional byPiece. note string | null totalCents int | null only for a walk-in sale with no items (manual lump-sum amount); mutually exclusive with items discountCents int, default 0 sale-level amount off the subtotal; only with items, and at most the subtotal

Validated server-side (SaleCreate.check_consistency): exactly one of items or totalCents must be provided, and buyerId presence must match saleType.

subtotalCents = the sum of line totals at the charged prices; totalCents = subtotalCents - discountCents. Each line snapshots listPriceCentsSnapshot (the product price at sale time), unitPriceCentsSnapshot (what was charged) and, server-side only, the unit cost. The cost is never returned to buyers.

Stock is validated for every line item (duplicate productIds aggregated first) before any of them are deducted — a multi-item sale either fully succeeds or fully fails.

Response: SaleRead (201). Errors: 404 (BuyerNotFoundError, ProductNotFoundError), 400 (InsufficientStockError, InvalidDiscountError).

POST /products/{id}/quick-sell takes the same optional unitPriceCents. The offline quick-sell queue stores the whole payload, so a replayed sale charges the agreed price.

docs.title: POST /sales/{saleId}/void and POST /sales/{saleId}/refund
docs.text:
Body: { reason?: string }. Both work only on a completed sale (otherwise 409), return every line's pieces to stock through apply_stock_change (reasons void / refund, with the sale_id), and set status, statusChangedAt and statusReason in one transaction.

  • Void means the sale was entered by mistake. It is excluded from every metric.
  • Refund means a real sale came back. It counts in gross sales and is subtracted as refundsCents.

Partial refunds are not supported. Response: SaleRead.

docs.title: POST /sales/{saleId}/proof
docs.text: Seller-only, multipart file (JPEG/PNG/WebP). Attaches or replaces the seller's photo of a walk-in customer's digital payment confirmation, stored privately like a buyer's screenshot and returned as paymentProofUrl. Only for completed walk_in sales (409 otherwise, and 409 for cash); 404 for another seller's sale; 400 for a bad image. The frontend calls it right after POST /sales when the seller took a photo on the QR screen. A failed upload never undoes the sale, and the receipt screen offers Add payment photo to try again. Response: SaleRead.

docs.title: POST /sales/{saleId}/confirm-payment and POST /sales/{saleId}/reject
docs.text:
Seller actions on a buyer's pending_payment order (409 for any other status).

  • Confirm payment (no body) sets status = completed. From then on the sale counts in every metric, linked to the buyer. A non-cash order needs a paymentProofUrl first (409 otherwise); a cash order is confirmed when the cash is handed over.
  • Reject (body { reason?: string }) sets status = cancelled and returns the reserved stock with cancel movements. Cancelled orders are excluded from every metric.

GET /sales?status=pending_payment lists the orders waiting for confirmation. SaleRead and SaleListItem carry paymentProofUrl / proofSubmittedAt; the public receipt never does.

In the frontend, sellers approve orders under New Sale → Buyer Account (/sales?path=account, with &order=<id> for one order, rendered by features/sales/OrderApproval.jsx). That tab shows a count of pending orders, the dashboard's PendingOrdersBanner links to it, and the chat order card for each order does too. Sellers can't add items to an order. Walk-in is the only kind of sale they ring up themselves.

docs.title: GET /sales
docs.text:
List/filter the caller's sales.

Query params: range (today|week|month|custom), start/end (required if range=custom), saleType, paymentMethod, buyerId, status, page, pageSize (max 100).

Response: SaleListResponse — { items: SaleListItem[], total, page, pageSize }. Each item includes a resolved buyerName (looked up separately, not stored on the sale) and itemCount.

The seller's Transactions page (/transactions, features/sales/TransactionsPage.jsx) lists these by date range. Its Delete transaction action calls the void endpoint, so the sale stays listed, marked Voided.

docs.title: GET /sales/receipt/{receiptCode}
docs.text:
Public, no auth. What the printed/QR receipt (/r/:receiptCode in the frontend) resolves to. Returns only public-safe fields — no buyer/seller IDs, emails, or phone numbers.

Response (PublicReceipt): businessName, receiptCode, saleType, items[] (name, quantity, unitType, unitPriceCents, lineTotalCents — all read from the sale_items snapshot columns, not the live product), subtotalCents, discountCents, totalCents, status (never the seller's statusReason), paymentMethod, createdAt.

docs.title: GET /sales/{saleId}
docs.text: Fetch one of the caller's sales by ID. 404 if not found or not owned. Response: SaleRead.

docs.title: Buyer-facing ordering & receipts (app/routers/catalog.py)
docs.text: These endpoints live in the catalog router file but call directly into services.sales.create_sale / read Sale rows, so they belong to this service conceptually.

docs.title: POST /catalog/products/{productId}/order
docs.text:
Auth: require_buyer. Places an itemized, buyer-linked order for a single product — the buyer version of ringing up a sale. Internally calls create_sale(sale_type=ITEMIZED, buyer_id=buyer.id, items=[(product_id, quantity)], status=PENDING_PAYMENT). Stock is deducted (reserved) right away, but the sale counts in no metric until the seller confirms payment (see Data Flow).

Request (BuyRequest): { quantity: int (>0), paymentMethod } Response: SaleRead (201, status: "pending_payment"). Errors: 400 (InsufficientStockError), 404 (product not found).

A cash order is reviewable straight away, so placing one also posts an order card into the buyer's chat with the seller.

docs.title: GET /me/orders/{saleId}
docs.text: Auth: require_buyer, scoped to the buyer's own orders (404 otherwise). Response: BuyerOrderRead — SaleRead plus sellerName and the seller's payoutAccounts, so the order page can show where to pay.

docs.title: POST /me/orders/{saleId}/proof
docs.text: Multipart file (JPEG/PNG/WebP). Attaches or replaces the payment screenshot on a pending, non-cash order and sets paymentProofUrl / proofSubmittedAt. Each upload posts an order card for the seller. Errors: 400 (not an image), 404 (not this buyer's order), 409 (order no longer pending, or a cash order).

docs.title: POST /me/orders/{saleId}/cancel
docs.text: The buyer withdraws a pending order: status → cancelled, stock returned with cancel movements. 409 if it is no longer pending.

docs.title: GET /me/receipts
docs.text:
Auth: require_buyer. Paginated purchase history for the current buyer.

Query: page, pageSize. Response: BuyerReceiptListResponse — each item includes sellerName, saleType, totalCents, status, paymentMethod, receiptCode, createdAt, itemCount.

docs.title: Related: analytics endpoints (app/routers/analytics.py)
docs.text:
Read-only aggregations over the same sales/products tables. Prefix /analytics, auth require_seller. The service is the package app/services/analytics/: sales.py (sales and profit), inventory.py (stock health and demand data), forecast.py (pure forecasting math) and insights.py (rules).

Business days. "Today", ranges and every daily, weekday or hourly bucket use local calendar days in settings.BUSINESS_TIMEZONE (default Asia/Manila), via app/core/business_time.py. Presets: today, week (the last 7 local days, including today) and month (the last 30). range=custom takes start/end as local YYYY-MM-DD dates, both inclusive.

Status rules. Voided, pending_payment and cancelled sales are invisible. Refunded sales count in gross sales and come back out as refundsCents. Net sales, transactions, units and profit come from completed sales only. COGS comes from the sale_items cost snapshots. costCoveragePct is the share of net sales that has a known cost, so a margin based on partial data is labelled as partial.

Method & path Description GET /analytics/summary Today's sale count/net sales, low-stock count, week-over-week change %. GET /analytics/overview?range=&start=&end= current and previous (the equal-length window just before) period metrics: gross sales at list price, price adjustments, discounts, refunds, net sales, transactions, units, average sale, COGS, gross profit, margin %, cost coverage %, plus changePct. Gross − adjustments − discounts − refunds = net. GET /analytics/top-products?range=&limit=&sort= Top products from completed sales, sort=revenue\|quantity\|profit. Profit is per line, before sale-level discounts. GET /analytics/sales-trend?range=&granularity= Net sales, sale count and gross profit per day|week|month bucket, zero-filled. GET /analytics/patterns?weeks=8 Average net sales and transactions per local weekday (Monday = 0) and per local hour. GET /analytics/inventory Per product: 7- and 30-day daily averages, days of stock left, suggested reorder (pieces for the next 14 days plus 3 days of safety stock), 30-day turnover, stock value at cost, and status (out_of_stock, stockout_risk = 7 days or less, low, slow_moving = no sale in 14 days, overstocked = more than 60 days, healthy). GET /analytics/forecast { accuracyPct, weekdayAdjusted, weekdayFactors, items[] }. Each item has forecast7/forecast14, method (history, fallback or none) and confidence. The rate is 0.6 × the 7-day average + 0.4 × the 30-day average, and products with fewer than 14 selling days use a low-confidence fallback. Weekday factors apply once the shop has 4 weeks of history. accuracyPct = 100 − WAPE of a backtest that forecasts last week from the data before it. GET /analytics/insights Rule-based { code, severity, action, params, productId }. The frontend translates code/action; params carries the figures (camelCase keys). Rules: stockout_risk, overstock, low_margin, below_cost, missing_cost, sales_spike/sales_drop (yesterday against the same weekday over 4 weeks), and emerging_bestseller. At most 3 per rule.

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text: Two sale paths share the same sales/sale_items schema and the same stock-deduction primitive (services.inventory.apply_stock_change), but are triggered from different UI surfaces and take slightly different code paths to get there.

docs.title: a) Walk-in sale
docs.text:
Triggered from the seller's New Sale screen on the Walk-in Sale tab (CheckoutPage). The seller taps product tiles to enter amounts on a number pad (QuantityPadSheet), can change a line's price for this sale (PriceEditor) and add a sale-level discount (CheckoutSummary), then taps Complete Sale. PaymentSheet asks how the buyer paid and shows the seller's matching payout QR for the customer to scan. Confirming sends POST /sales with saleType: "walk_in" and no buyerId.

flowchart TD
    A["Seller builds the cart on New Sale → Walk-in Sale"] --> B["Complete Sale → PaymentSheet<br/>(payment method + payout QR)"]
    B --> C["POST /sales (saleType=walk_in, items, discountCents)"]
    C --> D["Aggregate duplicate productIds;<br/>row-lock each product: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE"]
    D --> E{"Every line: stock_pieces − (quantity × piecesPerUnit) ≥ 0 ?"}
    E -- "No" --> F["Raise InsufficientStockError<br/>→ rollback → HTTP 400"]
    E -- "Yes" --> G["Deduct pieces for each line;<br/>write stock_movements rows (reason=sale)"]
    G --> H["Sale row: sale_type=walk_in, buyer_id=NULL, status=completed"]
    H --> I["sale_items snapshot: name, list and charged price, cost, unit at time of sale"]
    I --> J["Commit transaction"]
    J --> K["Receipt page; Transactions / Analytics<br/>(GET /sales, GET /analytics/*)"]

services/sales.create_sale validates stock for every line item first (aggregating duplicate product_ids), and only starts deducting once every line passes — so a multi-item cart either fully succeeds or fully fails, rather than partially selling out mid-checkout.

POST /products/{id}/quick-sell (services/inventory.quick_sell) is a single-product version of the same path that writes quick_sell movements. No screen uses it at the moment (see Inventory Service).

docs.title: b) Buyer-linked sale
docs.text:
Triggered from the buyer app's Buy button on a product detail page (BuySheet → POST /catalog/products/{id}/order), which calls the same services.sales.create_sale used by the seller's itemized checkout, with sale_type="itemized", buyer_id set to the authenticated buyer and status="pending_payment". The order reserves stock immediately but only becomes a counted sale once the seller confirms payment.

flowchart TD
    A["Buyer taps Buy on a product"] --> B["Enters quantity + payment method (BuySheet)"]
    B --> C["POST /catalog/products/{id}/order"]
    C --> D["Row-lock product: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE"]
    D --> E{"stock_pieces − (quantity × piecesPerUnit) ≥ 0 ?"}
    E -- "No" --> F["Raise InsufficientStockError<br/>→ rollback → HTTP 400"]
    E -- "Yes" --> G["Deduct pieces; write stock_movements row (reason=sale)"]
    G --> H["Sale row: sale_type=itemized, buyer_id=buyer.id,<br/>status=pending_payment"]
    H --> I["sale_items snapshot"]
    I --> J["Commit transaction"]
    J --> K["Buyer redirected to /buyer/orders/{saleId}"]
    K --> P{"Payment method"}
    P -- "GCash / Maya / bank" --> Q["Buyer uploads payment screenshot<br/>POST /me/orders/{id}/proof"]
    P -- "Cash" --> R["Buyer pays at pickup"]
    Q --> O["Order card posted in the buyer–seller chat<br/>(messages.sale_id)"]
    R --> O
    O --> S["Seller opens New Sale → Buyer Account<br/>(from the chat card or dashboard banner), views proof"]
    S -- "Confirm payment" --> T["status=completed<br/>→ counts in Sales History / Analytics, linked to buyer"]
    S -- "Reject" --> U["status=cancelled<br/>stock returned (reason=cancel)"]
    K -- "Buyer cancels" --> U

Note

Pending and cancelled orders never count in analytics. Analytics bucket a confirmed order by its created_at (when it was placed), not by when it was confirmed. The order card is posted by the backend (services/messages.post_order_card) once for a cash order and on every proof upload for a digital one. See Messaging Service.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
Public Market POS is a single FastAPI application (not separate microservices) whose routers delegate to distinct service modules — inventory, sales, messaging, payouts, catalog, analytics — all sharing one PostgreSQL database. The Seller and Buyer apps are two React route trees in the same frontend codebase, gated by role (ProtectedRoute role="seller"|"buyer" in App.jsx).

flowchart TB
    SellerApp["Seller App<br/>(React — /dashboard, /inventory, /sales,<br/>/transactions, /analytics, /profile)"]
    BuyerApp["Buyer App<br/>(React — /buyer, /buyer/products,<br/>/buyer/orders, /buyer/receipts)"]

    subgraph Backend["FastAPI backend — /api/v1"]
        Inventory["Inventory Service<br/>(app/routers/inventory.py + app/services/inventory.py)"]
        Sales["Sales Service<br/>(app/routers/sales.py + catalog.py + app/services/sales.py)"]
        Messaging["Messaging Service<br/>(app/routers/messages.py + app/services/messages.py)"]
        Payouts["Payout Accounts<br/>(app/routers/payouts.py + app/services/payouts.py)"]
    end

    DB[("PostgreSQL<br/>products, sales, sale_items, stock_movements,<br/>users, conversations, seller_payout_accounts")]

    SellerApp -->|"CRUD products, quick-sell, restock, photo upload"| Inventory
    SellerApp -->|"walk-in sales, approve orders,<br/>void/refund, receipts"| Sales
    SellerApp -->|"list/send messages"| Messaging
    SellerApp -->|"manage GCash/Maya/bank accounts + QR"| Payouts

    BuyerApp -->|"browse catalog, image search"| Inventory
    BuyerApp -->|"place order, upload proof, my receipts"| Sales
    BuyerApp -->|"message seller"| Messaging

    Sales -.->|"apply_stock_change() deducts stock<br/>in the same DB transaction"| Inventory
    Sales -.->|"post_order_card() when an order<br/>is ready for review"| Messaging
    Sales -.->|"order page shows the<br/>seller's payout accounts"| Payouts

    Inventory -->|"read/write"| DB
    Sales -->|"read/write"| DB
    Messaging -->|"read/write"| DB
    Payouts -->|"read/write"| DB

A few things worth calling out:

  • Catalog is buyer-facing inventory + sales, not a fourth service. app/routers/catalog.py reads Product rows (the same table Inventory owns) for browsing, and calls services.sales.create_sale directly for the POST /catalog/products/{id}/order endpoint (plus the /me/orders/... proof and cancel endpoints) — it is a thin façade over the other services, not an independent domain.
  • Sales never mutates stock directly. services/sales.create_sale, the void, refund, reject and cancel paths, and services/inventory.quick_sell all call services.inventory.apply_stock_change, which is the only function allowed to write Product.stock_pieces. That function row-locks the product (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE), rejects changes that would go negative, and writes an append-only stock_movements row — all in the same transaction as the sale.
  • Auth and Analytics aren't pictured above for clarity (one process per diagram) — auth issues JWTs consumed by every other router via get_current_user/require_seller/ require_buyer (app/core/deps.py), and analytics (the app/services/analytics/ package) is a read-only aggregation layer over the same sales/products tables the Sales and Inventory services own. It buckets days in settings.BUSINESS_TIMEZONE through app/core/business_time.py.
  • Uploads are shared. app/services/uploads.py validates and saves product photos, payout QR codes and payment screenshots to UPLOAD_DIR, which app/main.py serves at /uploads.

See Data Flow for the two sale paths in detail, and Unit Conversion for how stock_pieces behaves for piece, bundle and measure products.

docs.title: Unit Conversion
docs.text:
Product.stock_pieces is the single source of truth for stock, and it is always counted in individual pieces — regardless of whether the product is sold by the piece, by the bundle, or by weight. Product.pieces_per_unit is the conversion factor between "one selling unit" and "pieces deducted." Every stock change (quick-sell, itemized sale, restock) computes pieces = quantity × pieces_per_unit and passes that through services.inventory.apply_stock_change — nothing writes stock_pieces any other way.

flowchart LR
    A["Product defined<br/>unit_type + pieces_per_unit"] --> B["Sale input<br/>(bundle, piece, or measure quantity)"]
    B --> C["Conversion<br/>pieces = quantity × pieces_per_unit"]
    C --> D["Single stock count<br/>stock_pieces −= pieces"]
    D --> E["Stock re-displayed<br/>in the product's own unit_type"]

docs.title: Worked example — bundle
docs.text:
A seller lists pandesal as a bundle product with pieces_per_unit = 25 (one bundle = 25 pieces of bread) and stock_pieces = 250 (10 bundles on hand).

Step Value Buyer/seller sells 2 bundles Pieces deducted 2 × 25 = 50 New stock_pieces 250 − 50 = 200 Displayed remaining stock 200 / 25 = 8 bundles

ProductForm (frontend/src/features/inventory/ProductForm.jsx) labels this field "Pieces per Bundle" and only shows it for bundle products — piece and measure products always send pieces_per_unit = 1 and the field is hidden.

docs.title: Selling a bundle per piece
docs.text:
A sale line for a bundle product can set byPiece: true (SaleItemCreate.by_piece, and BuyRequest.by_piece for buyer orders). services.inventory.build_sale_item then snapshots it as a piece line: unit_type_snapshot = piece, list price and cost = per_piece_cents(price, pieces_per_unit) (integer half-up, so ₱100 / 3 = 3333 cents), and pieces_deducted = quantity. Receipts, void/refund/cancel and the forecast read the snapshot and pieces_deducted, so they need no special case. by_piece on a non-bundle product raises InvalidSaleUnitError (400). create_sale sums pieces_deducted per product across lines before deducting, so a bundle line and a piece line of the same product are validated together.

On the frontend, saleLineUnit(product, byPiece) in features/sales/salesFormat.js gives a line's price, cost and unit, and the New Sale cart keys lines by product and mode.

Analytics "units sold" still sums sale_items.quantity, so a piece line counts like a bundle there.

docs.title: Measured products
docs.text:
For unit_type = "measure" (meat by the kg, fabric by the yard, rope by the meter, …) the seller picks the unit, stored as Product.unit_label (≤ 16 chars, required for measure products). To allow fractional amounts without floats, everything quantity-shaped is stored in thousandths of that unit (MEASURE_QUANTITY_SCALE = 1000 in services/inventory.py):

Field Meaning for a measure product stock_pieces thousandths of the unit (50500 = 50.5 yd) low_stock_threshold thousandths of the unit sale / restock quantity thousandths of the unit (1500 = 1.5 yd) pieces_per_unit always 1 (enforced: 400 otherwise), so stock deducted = quantity price_cents per whole unit (12000 = ₱120/yd)

Line totals use line_total_cents(price_cents, quantity, unit_type) in services/inventory.py, which divides by the scale with integer half-up rounding (1500 × 12000 / 1000 = 18000). The frontend mirrors it as lineTotalCents in frontend/src/lib/format.js, alongside formatQuantity / parseQuantityInput / sanitizeQuantityInput for converting between the stored integer and the decimal text sellers type. sale_items.unit_label_snapshot keeps receipts stable if a product's unit label is edited later.

The migration c3e1a7d9f2b4 converted the old grams ("Per Kilo") type: grams were already thousandths of a kg, so stock and quantities were kept as-is, unit_label set to kg, and per-gram prices multiplied by 1000 to per-kg prices (line totals unchanged).

docs.title: Why this matters
docs.text: Because stock_pieces is always pieces, low-stock comparisons (stock_pieces <= low_stock_threshold), the demand forecast, and analytics all operate on one consistent unit regardless of how a product is sold — there is no unit-mismatch bug possible between "10 bundles low-stock" and "250 pieces low-stock" because the threshold is also stored in pieces.
